//subtext: Two typos in the KEY COMPETENCES table of the manuscript, both verified against the raw OOXML before being corrected here. 'DESCRIPTERS' is the table's own column header (the CDC syllabus and every other book in the family spell it DESCRIPTORS), and 'Problem Saving' is the competence the syllabus calls Problem Solving — neither is a Zambian spelling variant, both are slips. The 25 Oct manuscript adds front-matter and heading slips, each checked in its OOXML: the Acknowledgement calls this the "Form Four" Learner's Book; the Preface has "learner-centre approach" for learner-centred; Sub-topic 2.1.1 reads "Types of Books Prime Entry", the "of" dropped from the topic's own name, Books of Prime Entry; and the editor credit trails a run of dots after the name. Reading the whole book then found the slips listed after the first six entries: wrong words and agreement, "In this sub topic" against the SUB-TOPIC headings, a business renamed inside its own question (Chipata/Tionge, Lundazi/Mbuzi, Chanda/Waduka, Chanda/Chilembo), a Required line dated 2026 under a question dated 20X6 (or the reverse) - always brought to the question's own date - and the Topic 2.4 worked figures: Net Purchases drops the K11,000 carriage inwards its own formula adds, the cost-of-sales and gross-profit examples restate K480,000/K250,000 where the chain carries K491,000/K239,000, and the Waduka Farms illustration deducts a K10,000 that appears nowhere in its data (K345,000 + K25,000 - K140,000 = K230,000). Figures 7 and 9 were captioned 8 and 10 in the manuscript. "Returns inward(s)/outward(s)" is spelled four ways; the book's majority is the plural, as in Carriage inwards/outwards, so every form is first taken to the singular and then to the plural (a direct "inward"->"inwards" would double the s on the forms already right).

//coverImage: The cover picture the user chose (supplied as 10.jpeg, 853x1280). Converted to PNG and upscaled with Real-ESRGAN to 1800px wide, because 853px across the 144mm hero window is about 150 DPI against the 300 DPI print rule — 144mm needs 1701px. It is an accounting still life (ledgers, a columned cash book, a calculator, coin stacks and charts) with no people in it, so it depicts the subject but does not engage the disability-representation or gender-balance rules, which apply where human beings appear. NOTE: the source is 2:3 PORTRAIT and the hero window is 144x78mm (1.846:1 LANDSCAPE), filled with fit: "cover" — so the window keeps only a central horizontal band and the rest is cropped away.
//setMarker: Two roman sub-lists in the END OF TOPIC ASSESSMENT for Topic 2.5 printed with the wrong label. The manuscript types each as a SINGLE Word paragraph holding all of its items separated by line breaks and numbered as literal text ('i. Gross profit margin' / 'ii. Net profit margin' / …), under a parent part that ends in a colon. The importer models two list levels — a decimal top ('1.') and a lettered sub ('a)') — and has no third, so the first roman item was counted as one more letter in the lettered run and came out as 'e)' on printed p.134 and 'h)' on printed p.136, while its siblings stayed literal text underneath. The letters are plainly wrong (they read as further tasks rather than as the list the parent part introduces), so the marker is forced back to 'i.' in both. The remaining items still sit in the same paragraph as continuation lines; giving this manuscript shape a real third list level is an engine change, deliberately NOT attempted here.
